headline: This 2015 law requires the President to send Congress any Iran nuclear agreement and limits sanctions relief while Congress reviews it.
what_it_does: The law requires the President to send Congress the text of any nuclear agreement with Iran, along with verification reports and certifications, within five days of reaching it. During a review period, the President generally may not waive or reduce U.S. sanctions on Iran, and Congress can pass a resolution to block sanctions relief. The President must also report regularly on Iran's compliance and certify every 90 days whether Iran is meeting the agreement's terms.

who_it_affects.how: They receive the agreement, related reports, and regular compliance updates, and they get a review period to vote on whether to allow sanctions relief.

who_it_affects.group: The President and executive branch agencies, including the State Department
who_it_affects.how: They must transmit documents on deadlines, prepare verification assessments, report suspected Iranian violations, and certify compliance every 90 days.

who_it_affects.group: Companies and individuals subject to U.S. sanctions on Iran
who_it_affects.how: Sanctions relief is restricted during the review period, so existing sanctions generally stay in place while Congress considers an agreement.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on May 22, 2015.
